particularites.text: Major leadership transition: Tim Cook steps down as CEO on 31/08/2026 (last earnings call on 30/07/26) and becomes executive Chairman of the board; John Ternus (SVP Hardware Engineering, at Apple for nearly 20 years) becomes CEO on 01/09/2026 - i.e. at the very start of fiscal year 2027. Transition presented as the outcome of long-term succession planning, unanimously approved by the board. No strategy change announced at this stage; to be monitored closely at the next refresh (first full quarter under Ternus's leadership).

Active and regular share buyback programme running for more than a decade (62,1 Md$ repurchased in the first 9 months of fiscal 2026 alone) combined with an established quarterly dividend (0,27$/share) - justifies applying the '0% yield' branch of rule E5-a bis to net cash (cash is treated as consumed by the buybacks rather than generating a modelled financial income).

ownership.insiderDesc: Very low, typical of a mega-cap with no founder in the capital. Tim Cook (outgoing CEO) holds ~3,3M shares (~1 Md$ at the current price), very largely arising from performance RSUs; periodic sales for diversification/tax purposes. New CEO John Ternus: stake not yet publicly documented at this stage.

notableHolders.movement: stable - remains Berkshire's largest equity position (~23% of the listed portfolio) despite earlier partial sales; handover of the Berkshire CEO role to Greg Abel in January 2026, Buffett remains Chairman.

ownership.coverageNote: Shareholder base overwhelmingly institutional/index-based (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street, etc.) - few distinct high-conviction active managers beyond Berkshire in the Omnium watch list.

items.title: DOJ v. Apple - federal antitrust complaint (21/03/2024) alleging monopolisation of the smartphone markets ('performance smartphones' and 'smartphones') through App Store rules, developer restrictions and control of key iPhone features.
items.allegedBy: US Department of Justice + plusieurs Etats/procureurs generaux
items.outcome: Discovery under way since April 2026; preliminary settlement negotiations opened (July 2026), with Apple having made several proposals covering 4 of the 5 categories of DOJ grievances - Apple Watch/Android interoperability remains the main sticking point. Outcome not determinable at this stage; potentially resolved before the CEO transition of 01/09/26.
items.source: Depot judiciaire federal (New Jersey), TechTimes, 10-Q T2 2026

items.title: European Commission DMA fine (500 M euros, 23/04/2025) for restricting App Store developers from redirecting users towards cheaper purchases outside the App Store; DMA 'gatekeeper' designation upheld by the EU General Court on 08/07/2026 (Apple's appeal dismissed).
items.outcome: Fine under appeal before the European courts, still pending. The confirmation of gatekeeper status (07/2026) closes off part of Apple's options for contesting the interoperability required by the DMA.

items.title: Epic Games v. Apple - contempt proceedings before the US Supreme Court, tied to enforcement of the App Store anti-steering injunction.
items.outcome: Proceedings still active; adds to the stack of regulatory litigation (DOJ, DMA, UK class action) inherited by the new CEO.

compliance.note: Unusually dense regulatory stack for this refresh (DOJ + DMA + Epic + UK class action simultaneously) - to be monitored as a priority at the next refresh, in particular any DOJ resolution before/after John Ternus takes office.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: Q4 FY26: total revenue +9% to +11% YoY, embedding ~2.5pts sequential FX headwind and a significant sequential increase in supply constraints (iPhone, Mac AND iPad). iPhone mid-teens reported growth; Services roughly in line with Q3 after ~2.5pts FX. Gross margin 47-48% (incl. ~1pt of expected tariff refunds), OpEx $19.1-19.4B, OI&E ~$350M ex-MTM, tax ~16.5%.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: No annual guidance (constant practice). No color beyond September explicitly (Reitzes exchange); the adjusted sequential GM decline (~160bp to ~46.5% mid-range) is >100% memory-cost driven, FX minimal.
pointsCles: Q3 FY26 revenue $109.4B (+16% YoY, June-quarter record, beat ~$457M) with June records in EVERY geographic segment; EPS $2.02 (+29%) beat by $0.13 but includes +$0.11 of tariff refunds - recurring base ~$1.91 (bridged in quarterlyEPS); GM 50.1% incl ~2pts of refunds (mid-guidance without them); OCF $34.4B, all three metrics June records even ex-refunds.

Supply becomes THE constraint: advanced-node SoC availability, root cause being demand ABOVE plan (iPhone +22% to $54.3B, Mac +29% to $10.4B, both June records) with an unusually inflexible supply chain; Q4 constraints increase significantly and extend to iPhone, Mac and iPad - explicitly a demand-forecast problem, not a supplier problem (Arizona fab >100M components this year).

Memory '100-year flood': costs paid rose again sequentially and rise further in Q4, driving reluctant price increases on iPad and Mac; offsets (carry-in inventory - decreasing after September, cheaper non-memory components, mix) only partial; DRAM = 3 suppliers, all sourcing options under evaluation; beyond September market pricing keeps climbing - the key margin swing factor.

Last Tim Cook call - John Ternus takes over September 1 (present on the call); Siri AI betas exceptionally well received, EU launch pending Commission talks (Mac exempt from DMA scope), China approval obtained for base Apple Intelligence features with Siri AI to follow; monetization via iCloud+ upsell; Apple Upgrade hardware leasing launched in US retail with Klarna; Broadcom >$30B American Manufacturing agreement; $33B returned in the quarter (buybacks $25.8B), cash $147B vs debt $84B.

hypothese.summary: Record June quarter on every front (revenue 109,4 Md$ +16%, EPS 2,02$ +29%, driven by iPhone +22% and Mac +29%), but two structural signals to watch: (1) memory cost inflation described as the 'flood of the century' by Tim Cook, which will compress gross margin in Q4 FY26 (guided at 47-48% against 50,1% reported, of which ~1pt of non-recurring tariff refunds) and potentially beyond; (2) a historic leadership transition - this was Tim Cook's last call as CEO, with John Ternus taking over on 01/09/2026. The Omnium model excludes the one-off tariff benefit (0,11$ in Q3) and treats net cash as consumed by the regular buybacks (E5-a bis, no financial income modelled). omniumEPS 8,78->14,21 (FY2026-FY2030).
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Refresh on a record June quarter (Q3 FY26): revenue 109.4bn (+16%), iPhone 54.3bn (+22%, record), Mac +29% (MacBook Neo), Services 30.7bn (+12%, record though slightly under consensus), EPS 2.02 (+29%). Published gross margin 50.1% includes ~2pts of one-off tariff refunds (EPS +0.11) which the Omnium normalized base EXCLUDES. The key prospective signal: the CFO quantified AI-driven memory-cost inflation (DRAM/NAND) as the main FY27 margin headwind.

== THESIS READ ==
- The iPhone supercycle is real (foldable + AI features), but FY27 margins face the memory-cost wall management itself quantified. Watch: gross-margin guidance each quarter as the headwind lands.
- Services growth (+12%) slightly under consensus for a second time - the multiple's key support. Watch: App Store regulatory outcomes and Google-TAC dependency.
- First full quarter under John Ternus's leadership approaches. Watch: capital-allocation and AI-strategy signals.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Fiscal year ends September (FY26 = Oct 25-Sep 26). Base = normalized GAAP: tariff refunds excluded; FY24 net retreated +10.2bn (EU State Aid reversal, E5 d-bis). E5-a bis convention: 0% yield on the ~62bn net cash (perpetual-buyback issuer) - finNet=0 by construction in the bridge.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
Revenue +9/10%/yr; EBIT margin ~32.3% held (memory headwind vs mix); ETR 16.5% normative (FY25 actual 15.8%, +0.9bn documented residual); shares -3%/yr (~62bn bought back in 9M FY26). Watch: memory-cost pass-through; Services deceleration; Vision/wearables contribution.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q4 FY26 (Oct) + FY27 framing; iPhone cycle sell-through; App Store rulings; Ternus's first strategic moves.

ancrages.moteur: Reported FY2024 net income (93 736 M$) included a unique exceptional tax charge of 10,2 Md$ tied to the payment under the EU-Ireland 'State Aid' decision (upheld by the European Court of Justice on 10/09/2024) - a genuine tax one-off, non-recurring -> 2024 data adjusted to 103 936 M$ (E5 d-bis) to avoid a false step in reading the historical trajectory.

Memory (DRAM/NAND) cost inflation described as the 'flood of the century' by the CEO, explaining >100% of the sequential gross margin compression in Q3 FY26 (49,3%->48,1% ex-tariffs) and guided down again in Q4 (46,5% ex-tariffs) - DRAM market concentrated among 3 suppliers, duration uncertain -> FY2026-2027 margin trajectory built with continued pressure, gradual recovery assumed from FY2028 as memory supply adjusts.

One-off tariff refunds identified in Q3 FY26 (~2pts of margin, +0,11$ EPS) and guided in Q4 FY26 (~1pt of margin) - same type of non-recurring item already excluded at Amazon and Boston Scientific this cycle -> excluded from the Omnium FY2026 normalised base.

Active and regular share buyback programme running for more than a decade (62,1 Md$ in the first 9 months of FY2026 alone, a track record of several consecutive years) -> rule E5-a bis, '0% yield' branch applied: net cash (~62 Md$ at end-June 2026) is treated as consumed by the buybacks, no financial income modelled over the projection horizon.

Normative tax rate set at 16,5%, consistent with the CFO's explicit guidance for Q4 FY26 and the recent effective rate (15,61% reported FY2025, 17,58% over the first 9 months of FY2026) - midpoint of the range retained for the whole projection horizon.

Recent buyback pace (62,1 Md$ over 9 months of FY2026, an annualised run-rate very close to recent years) -> extrapolated at -3%/yr on omniumShares across the whole horizon, consistent with the trend observed FY2023-FY2026 (15 813M -> ~14 650M).

CEO transition (Cook -> Ternus, 01/09/2026) treated as neutral for the quantified trajectory at this stage: planned long-term succession, an engineering/product profile close to the existing Apple culture, no strategy change announced. To be reassessed at the next refresh once the first full quarter under Ternus has been reported (Q1 FY2027).

2025.residualNote: FY25 effective tax 15.8% vs 16.5% normative (+0.9bn favorable gap). No financial income is modeled on the net cash (~62bn) per the E5-a bis rule (0% yield convention for perpetual-buyback issuers) - finNet=0 by construction. FY24 'data' net already retreated +10.2bn for the EU State Aid one-off (documented in-fiche).
